selection_note: UPSTREAM UPGRADE BATCH 23, explicit operator size ten. Next ten included Index S1=A/S2=C assessment source identities by reviewed_at descending, source-disjoint from all 125 sources in integrated batches 01-22 and from current open Upstream/Index PR titles and source claims checked at intake. Exact canonical Index main pinned; prospective hypotheses checkpointed before inspecting fresh target code, issues or PRs. Screening questions are not defect, benefit, runner or external-publication claims.

candidates.finding: Check whether two supported Web requests for the same durable conversation instantiate separate ConversationService mutexes and admit overlapping load/run/persist sections, despite the worker-scoped keyed mutex.
candidates.screening_result: Web route constructs a new ConversationService for each request backed by a shared store; KeyedMutex is allocated per service instance. Overlapping same-conversation requests plausibly bypass local critical-section coordination, but supported multi-instance deployment semantics and a first-party concurrent request reproducer were not established. Static screen only.
candidates.blocker: Require a bounded supported two-request same-conversation native fixture and an accepted single-worker versus cross-worker locking scope before a safe source-native change.

candidates.finding: Check whether cancellation or failure during delegated domain-agent execution can skip ephemeral session-map cleanup or overwrite the caller's retained agent/session, despite the normal unique-key isolation path.
candidates.screening_result: A failure in _dispatch_single_runtime escapes before the post-dispatch removal of the ephemeral delegation session. Distinct dev-alpha-2 native runner f540ff69-d09f-4249-9b0a-37505e1e0d03 checked exact source 4f34d57: baseline 11 passed, 1 failed (leaked delegate key); same fixture after try/finally fix 12 passed, 0 failed; git diff --check PASS. No model/provider call and no external PR.
candidates.observed_native_change: Separate dev-alpha-2 SSH runner session f540ff69-d09f-4249-9b0a-37505e1e0d03: exact first-party 4f34d57, matched pytest tests/test_delegation_session_isolation.py, before 11/12 PASS, after 12/12 PASS. Receipt records host and two patch hashes.

candidates.finding: Check whether a supported nested team or background worker tool fails to inherit the per-agent worktree cwd and writes to the shared parent checkout while another worker edits the same file.
candidates.screening_result: InProcessBackend.spawn launches a worker task without setting its worktree_path as the task-context cwd, unlike the process teammate path. Distinct dev-alpha-2 native runner fa81ce8f-dfdc-4046-8194-3df5e5437271 checked exact source 34a2d55: baseline 8 passed, 1 failed (parent cwd inherited); after scoped with_cwd around launch 9 passed, 0 failed. No model/provider call or external PR.
candidates.observed_native_change: Separate dev-alpha-2 SSH runner session fa81ce8f-dfdc-4046-8194-3df5e5437271: exact first-party 34a2d55, matched pytest tests/test_team_backend.py, before 8/9 PASS, after 9/9 PASS; one harmless pytest config warning. Receipt records host and patch hashes.

candidates.finding: Check whether the one-shot staged dependent-code dispatch can be scheduled twice when parallel solver completions merge status/intermediate-results in different orders, violating its documented single follow-up hop.
candidates.screening_result: The staged dependent-code dispatch uses a state marker to prevent a repeat hop in the reviewed coordinator graph. No native two-completion route demonstrating a second scheduling was substantiated; close this exact double-hop prediction without changing source. Static review only.

candidates.finding: Check whether cancellation or a failed approval/tool call while holding the shared propose-approve-apply mutation gate strands a sibling editor, rather than releasing the gate and returning a recoverable failure.
candidates.screening_result: Mutation protection enters Python's threading.RLock via a with context. Ordinary exceptions release the gate through context-manager exit; the predicted permanent stranded gate was not demonstrated. Static close, no native fault-injection claim.

candidates.finding: Check whether concurrent Tool_Agent insertions into the capacity-bounded API pool can evaluate sufficiency or global stop on a stale snapshot, returning contradictory stop/continue feedback after the insertion lock is released.
candidates.screening_result: First-party threaded Tool_Agent path holds counter_lock around pool insertion, sufficiency assessment and global stop bookkeeping. The suggested stale-snapshot interleave within this protected region is unavailable; no live LLM sufficiency request was executed.

candidates.finding: Check whether a second scheduler tick can refire a still-inflight due job before its per-job last_run/retry state is persisted, while the anti-starvation concurrent dispatcher correctly runs unrelated due jobs.
candidates.screening_result: Scheduler.run awaits the full tick; each tick awaits its due _fire tasks before the next scheduler tick. A second overlapping automatic tick firing the same in-flight job was not supported by that loop. Manually invoked run_now is a different path, outside the frozen question.

candidates.finding: Check whether two worker worktree completions racing a dirty-parent transition can each pass an unguarded cleanliness check and attempt conflicting base-workspace merge despite the serialized merge lock.
candidates.screening_result: The code acquires base_merge_lock before parent_workspace_is_dirty and retains it throughout the sequential merge. The proposed two-worker check/merge race was not corroborated. Dirty-parent state is recorded and worker branches preserved.

candidates.finding: Check whether an interrupted ticket claim after atomic remote branch creation but before ledger/live-marker update strands ownership or allows a second claimant to start, defeating the single-accepted-ticket feedback path.
candidates.screening_result: Current default branch differs from assessed 9a2fc16. First-party remote branch creation is the atomic ticket claim; ledger bookkeeping can be interrupted and rollback can fail, plausibly leaving an orphaned branch. The split-brain second-claim scenario is not established because the remote branch still blocks another claim. No safe autonomous orphan reclamation policy established.
candidates.blocker: Need a pinned interrupted-claim native fixture and maintainer-approved orphaned-claim recovery semantics; do not delete a remotely held claim on conjecture.

candidates.finding: Check whether a preempted or denied low-tier actuator dispatch incorrectly consumes cooldown and suppresses a subsequent allowed high-tier action for the same commissioned resource in the next supported event cycle.
candidates.screening_result: At the current source head, dispatch_plan defines cooldown consumption separately from refused/preempted outcomes; dispatch_coordinator does not charge the forbidden outcome as a successful cooldown in the preregistered path. No demonstrated suppression of the next permitted high-tier dispatch.
